expectations.text: Rejects plain Secrets in Git, and states that base64 is encoding not encryption — anyone with repo read access has the credential

expectations.text: Notes that External Secrets Operator / Vault keep the secret out of Git entirely, whereas Sealed Secrets and SOPS commit an encrypted form
expectations.evidence: ESO: 'Git holds only a reference ... no ciphertext in Git at all'; Vault CSI: no Secret object at all; Sealed Secrets commits the encrypted SealedSecret and SOPS commits encrypted values in place.

expectations.text: Mentions that Argo CD needs to be able to decrypt or resolve whichever mechanism is chosen
expectations.evidence: States SOPS 'requires a CMP in the repo-server' to decrypt during sync, and makes the secret controller a sync-wave prerequisite so Argo CD resolves the Secret before the Deployment.

expectations.text: Does not simply say 'use Sealed Secrets' without stating why it fits or does not fit their situation
expectations.evidence: Recommends ESO specifically for DB credentials because rotation needs no Git commit, and qualifies Sealed Secrets as acceptable only if there is no vault, with 'rotation is a pull request' stated as the accepted cost.

expectations.text: Compares the real options rather than asserting one — app-of-apps, ApplicationSet, monorepo, multi-repo, environment-branch — with trade-offs
expectations.evidence: Compares two repos vs six per-service repos, directory overlays vs environment branches, ApplicationSet vs hand-written Applications, and app-of-apps (bootstrap only) vs ApplicationSet, each with a stated reason in the decision table.

expectations.text: Recommends ApplicationSet for the 6 services x 3 envs x 2 clusters fan-out instead of hand-maintained Application manifests, and explains that generators remove the per-combination manifest
expectations.evidence: ApplicationSets replace the 36 hand-written Applications ('Add a directory, get an Application'), with a matrix/list generator fan-out across env and cluster and a cluster generator for addons.

expectations.text: Separates platform/cluster addons from application workloads (different ownership, different review path, often a different AppProject)
expectations.evidence: platform-config (platform team) is separated from app-config (service teams) on ownership, with distinct AppProjects (platform vs services-<env>) and prod-specific destinations and sync windows.

expectations.text: Addresses environment promotion explicitly — directory-per-env vs branch-per-env — and notes the trade-off rather than silently picking one
expectations.evidence: 'Environments are directories, not branches' with the reasoning (branches drift silently, generate merge conflicts, do not scale past ~3 environments) and a RollingSync dev-staging-prod promotion ordering.

expectations.text: Warns against targetRevision: HEAD for production regardless of pattern chosen
expectations.evidence: targetRevision: HEAD is never mentioned. The generated Applications track targetRevision: main and there is no warning against HEAD or guidance to pin a tag/digest for production.

expectations.text: Flags at least one anti-pattern relevant to their current layout (e.g. a flat directory of hand-edited Applications does not scale, or mixing platform and tenant resources in one AppProject)
expectations.evidence: 'What you have, and why it hurts' flags the flat directory of hand-edited Applications and that platform addons and app config share one blast radius and one set of reviewers.
